issues.title: [Bug]: PD failing at long context/bigger batches
issues.body:
### Bug Report

Hi,

I'm currently testing the PD performance in SGLang at larger batches. The motivation being, this is a worker profile I expect to encounter in (agentic) chat. I think there is some error, but I struggle to identify the source based on the available logs. 

Steps to replicate on a single H100 node (should also work with less compute if you change the TP size/smaller model):

`run_decode.sh`
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8 --disaggregation-mode decode --port 30001 --host 10.1.0.21 --tp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2
```

`run_prefill.sh`
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8 --disaggregation-mode prefill --port 30000 --host 10.1.0.21 --tp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e5m2
```

`run_proxy.sh`
```bash
python3 -m sglang.srt.disaggregation.mini_lb --prefill http://10.1.0.21:30000 --decode http://10.1.0.21:30001 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002
```

For a single simple setup this works fine, the problem starts when I try to simulate a batch of long context, e.g. 8x30k tokens in. Than it completely fails

```py
import asyncio
import aiohttp
import json

async def send_request(session, request_id):
    # Generate ~30k tokens of text (roughly 120k characters)
    large_text = "This is a sample sentence for load testing. " * 2500
    
    payload = {
        "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-32B-FP8",
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "system",
                "content": "You are a helpful assistant."
            },
            {
                "role": "user", 
                "content": large_text
            }
        ],
        "max_tokens": 100,
        "temperature": 0.7
    }
    
    async with session.post(
        "http://10.1.0.21:8002/v1/chat/completions",
        json=payload,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    ) as response:
        result = await response.json()
        print(f"Request {request_id} completed: {response.status}")
        return result

async def main():
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        tasks = [send_request(session, i) for i in range(1, 32)]
        results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
        print(f"All {len(results)} requests completed")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

The first few requests complete fine:

```bash
Request 1 completed: 200
Request 2 completed: 200
Request 3 completed: 200
Request 4 completed: 200
Request 5 completed: 200
```

but later it just stalls. 

The workers than fail to give any further responses. Errors:

I identified this error while running my [benchmarking suite](https://github.com/tugot17/tokenomics), but the above simplified setup also causes the same problem; hence, I included it as it is easier to replicate. It seems something under the hood fails when the KV cache size grows above some threshold.

Any ideas what might be an issue?

linked_prs.title: docs: add troubleshooting steps for QP allocation error
linked_prs.body: Record the problem and the solution mentioned in #691. Thanks @tugot17 to report this.

ai_judgment.response: Yes. The issue involves failures related to LLM operation, specifically exceeding context length thresholds and potential mismanagement of KV cache size, which aligns with the "Context length issues" sub-category under LLM operation issues in the agent issue taxonomy.
